headline: School committee to consider bus lease purchase, a support staff contract, an emergency fire alarm expenditure, and an energy efficiency Phase 2 project.
summary: The committee will take up final approval of a bus lease purchase and first approval of a 2026 to 2029 support staff contract. It will also consider an emergency fire alarm expenditure and Energy Efficiency Phase 2, plus staff nominations and an executive session on contract negotiations.

School Board Professional Development - The Maine School Boards Association (MSBA) 
affirms its commitment to promoting high-quality governance training and the adoption of 
best practices as foundational to effective school board service throughout the State of 
Maine. MSBA strongly encourages all newly elected and appointed school board members to 
participate in orientation and foundational governance training at the earliest practicable 
opportunity following the commencement of their service, and encourages member boards to 
establish local expectations and policies that support such participation. MSBA encourages 
all school board members — regardless of tenure — to engage in ongoing professional 
development throughout their service, and recognizes that effective governance is a 
continuous practice that benefits from regular learning, reflection, and collaboration with 
peers; MSBA identifies the following as core areas of knowledge and practice essential to 
effective school board governance, and will work to ensure that training opportunities 
address each of these areas: 
• The distinct and complementary roles of the school board and the superintendent, and the 
importance of maintaining a productive and professional working relationship between 
them; 
• Policy development, adoption, and oversight as the primary instrument of board 
governance; 
• Budget development, financial oversight, and the responsible stewardship of public 
funds; 
• Maine education law, including the requirements of Title 20-A of the Maine Revised 
Statutes, and the legal obligations of school board members;
• The Freedom of Access Act 
• Parliamentary Procedure  
• School board Self-evaluation 
• On-boarding of school board members 
• Collective bargaining processes and the board's role in labor relations; 
• Ethical conduct, conflict of interest, and the responsibilities of public office; 
• Community engagement, transparency, and building public trust in local educational 
governance 
MSBA will develop, expand, and continually improve its training programs, resources, and 
peer learning opportunities to serve the diverse needs of member boards across Maine, 
including boards in rural, small, and under-resourced districts.
